summary.name: CoCounsel
summary.one_liner: CoCounsel is Thomson Reuters' AI assistant for legal, tax, audit, compliance, and drafting professionals, marketed under the "Fiduciary-Grade AI" label and formerly branded through Casetext.
use_cases: managing large document sets for litigation
verifying AI answers before client advice
summary.what_it_does: CoCounsel is an AI product from Thomson Reuters aimed at professionals in legal, tax, audit, compliance, and drafting work. The page says its answers are grounded in Thomson Reuters' proprietary authoritative content (including Westlaw, Practical Law, and Checkpoint) and that it surfaces sources and reasoning so users can verify outputs. It connects to Microsoft 365 and some document management system partners. The page states that prompts are restricted to a defined set of verified content, that customer data is not used to train models, and that data is encrypted with TLS 1.2 in transit and AES-256 at rest. Hosting is stated as U.S.-based, with region-based hosting listed for the UK, Australia, and Canada.
notable: Grounded in Thomson Reuters proprietary legal and tax content such as Westlaw and Practical Law
Surfaces sources and reasoning so outputs can be verified
Customer prompts and content are stated not to be used for model training; zero-retention API calls to LLM providers
Data hosting described as U.S.-based with regional options in UK, Australia, and Canada
caveats: The listing marks it as paid, and the page itself offers no public pricing
Region-based hosting is listed only for the UK, Australia, and Canada
The page says it supports human judgment and does not replace professionals' responsibility for their work
